title: Silas and the Thorn
premise: Mirabel Nystrom, a royal food-taster who has spent years dosing himself with poison to stay useful and unnoticed, secretly keeps the ledgers of the Gilded Thorn, a guild that trades in impossible things. When a mute child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Mirabel recognizes it from a ledger entry he was ordered to burn: a soul sold decades ago to the court beneath the mountain, and the child is that soul's last living echo. To save her, he must betray both his guild and the crown that owns his life, descending into the mountain court with nothing but forged entries, borrowed names, and the loyalty of the found family he never admitted he had. He wins her back by trading his own name into the ledger—erasing himself from every record and memory—but the child, remembering him when no one else can, writes him back into existence by hand.
about_author: Coral Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging trade ledgers from defunct merchant guilds before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people whose work keeps them invisible, and lives near a harbor where the fog rolls in on schedule.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. We meet him mid-routine: tasting the queen's breakfast, recording doses in his private ledger, then slipping across town to balance accounts for the Gilded Thorn. A child appears at the guild door at closing, speaking a language no one knows—except Mirabel, who has seen its script in an entry he was ordered to burn. Emotional beat: quiet dread as invisibility begins to fail him.

chapters.title: What Was Sold Beneath
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, with interludes from the child's fragmented memories. He deciphers the burned entry: forty years ago, a mother sold her unborn daughter's soul to the mountain court for a harvest that saved the city. The child is that debt come due, and collectors arrive at the guild demanding delivery. The guildmaster orders Mirabel to hand her over. Emotional beat: loyalty fractures—he refuses, forging a ledger line to hide her.

chapters.title: The Court Under the Mountain
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Mirabel and the child, now named Wren. Hunted by both crown agents and guild enforcers, they descend through abandoned mine-shafts into the mountain court, where debts are currency and Mirabel's double life becomes his weapon: he can read every contract ever filed there. Climax: facing the court's registrar, he offers the only thing of value—a taster's body saturated with forty poisons, proof of a life spent paying others' prices—and trades his name for Wren's soul.

chapters.title: Written Back
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, then Mirabel's. They surface to find the world has forgotten Mirabel: the guild's books show blank pages, the palace has another taster, even his own handwriting looks foreign to him. But Wren, bound to him by the traded soul, remembers. In the guild's back room she takes up a pen and writes his name into the ledger herself—an act no contract anticipated. Emotional beat: bittersweet restoration; he returns not invisible but chosen, family made explicit at last.
